description: EERI's Learning From Earthquakes (LFE) programme, formally started in 1973 and funded largely by the U.S. National Science Foundation, sends multidisciplinary teams of earth scientists, engineers and social scientists to investigate damaging earthquakes, and compiles their data into reports kept in the LFE Reconnaissance Archive. Teams usually deploy within several days and spend one to two weeks in the field; EERI shares responsibility for U.S. reconnaissance with the USGS and leads international missions, and the World Bank's GFDRR has supported teams in developing countries. A recent example: after the Mw 7.2 and 7.5 earthquakes in northern Venezuela on 24 June 2026, an LFE team surveyed La Guaira and Caracas from 17 to 27 August 2026, inspecting housing, a hospital and a bus terminal and deploying accelerometers and LiDAR scanners, as reported on 17 September 2026. Coverage: damaging earthquakes worldwide since the 1970s. Access: public reports and news; archive website linked from EERI. Licence: EERI terms. Caveats: reports are rapid qualitative surveys, not systematic damage censuses. Simulation uses are damage observations for validating building fragility and earthquake scenario models. Related records: the DesignSafe Data Depot and StEER reconnaissance.
